clue.text: Range of service provided

parts.note: Mass is a church service
'provided' means on condition that, i.e. if

explanation.surface: Someone asks what variety of service is on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, a mountain range in geography.

clue.text: Somewhat more unusual addition to family

definitions.meaning: a bit odder, i.e. slightly more strange
a coy old phrase for a baby on the way

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular euphemism for an expected baby, and literally means rather odder.

clue.text: See 21
Old Bob's third protection inadequate for 18's land?

indicators.note: 18 is Spooner, so in his land the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: poor means inadequate
a fence is a protective barrier

explanation.surface: A third-rate barrier seems a poor deal in some reverend's country.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob is the old British shilling, twelve old pennies, so a third of one is four old pence. Swapping the starts of 'poor fence' gives the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A shilling (bob) was twelve pence, so its third was a coin of four old pennies.

clue.text: Ex-president's idea of African primate

parts.note: George Bush, a former US president
one's 'baby' is a pet idea or project

explanation.surface: A former president's concept of a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the possessive just joins the president to his brainchild.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushbaby, or galago, is a small nocturnal primate of African forests.

clue.text: Meat and drink makes 18's Irish criminal live

indicators.note: 18 is Spooner, so the opening sounds of the two words are exchanged

parts.note: thief as spoken in an Irish accent, 'teef'
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A dish and a drink turn an Irish crook into someone who lives well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish criminal' plays on the Irish pronunciation of thief as 'teef'; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef tea is a broth made from meat, drunk as a hot restorative.

clue.text: Pervert, like this stunner

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mean 'written like this'
a knockout (KO) is a stunning blow

explanation.surface: A deviant is compared to a gorgeous person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicko is slang for a sick-minded or perverted person.

clue.text: Second arrivals at fictitious castle with imperial 11?

parts.note: B is the second letter, as in grade B
landings are aircraft arrivals

explanation.surface: Late arrivals at a storybook castle with a regal hog house.
explanation.walkthrough: Blandings Castle is in P.G. Wodehouse's comic novels; its prize sow, the Empress of Blandings, lives in a sty (11).
explanation.definitionFit: Wodehouse's fictional castle houses the Empress, a pig, so it has an imperial sty.

clue.text: Refuted Thatcher when 18 put indication on water carrier

indicators.note: 18 is Spooner, so his version swaps the opening sounds of the main words

parts.note: marked the means put a sign on the item
a bucket carries water

explanation.surface: Contradicting the Prime Minister when a vicar labels a pail.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher famously said 'you can't buck the market'; doing so refutes her. Spooner swaps M and B in 'marked the bucket'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatcher declared the market could not be bucked, so having done it disproves her claim.

clue.text: Tie decoy around one with gun

indicators.note: the decoy's letters are wrapped around the next pieces

parts.note: a lure is a decoy
I is the Roman numeral one
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Binding a decoy duck around a hunter carrying a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligature is a cord or thread used to tie something, such as a blood vessel.

clue.text: It could be an excellent object, which ancestors have concealed

definitions.text: It could be an excellent object

indicators.note: the forebears' words keep the answer tucked inside them

explanation.surface: A treasured heirloom that the forebears kept hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a chance can be 'excellent', and the clue invites a precious object instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An opportunity is something that can be fine or excellent, as in an excellent prospect.

clue.text: Facial problem whence squealing may be heard

indicators.note: the word for a pig's home is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a sty is a pigpen, from which squealing comes

explanation.surface: An ailment of the face from which shrieks emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a minor facial complaint.

clue.text: Form of pasta for 18 not dogs

indicators.note: 18 is Spooner, so the first letters of the two words are traded

parts.note: taken as written
poodles are a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Insisting the dish served is pasta and not dog meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot Noodle is a British brand of instant noodles sold in a pot, loosely a pasta snack.

clue.text: Divorce centre given points for glory

parts.note: Reno, Nevada, was famous for quick divorces
W, west, is a compass point
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A city known for divorces is awarded marks for its fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame or celebrity, a near synonym of glory.

clue.text: With increasingly 'igh temperature, be on fire for battle

parts.note: hotter, said with the aitch dropped as the apostrophe shows
to burn is to be on fire

explanation.surface: As things get hotter, the fire really takes hold before the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'igh signals the dropped aitch, so hotter loses its H. Otterburn (1388) was a battle between the English and Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Otterburn was fought in Northumberland between Scots and English in 1388.

clue.text: One time dimension in due course

parts.note: a means one
length is a dimension

explanation.surface: A physics remark about time as one of the dimensions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, after a long while, as does in due course.

clue.text: Burden island with logger

parts.note: to lumber someone is to burden them
the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Saddling an island with a tree-feller.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumberman fells and processes trees for timber, as does a logger.

clue.text: Good guy speaks but isn't fluent

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good person
utters means speaks

explanation.surface: A decent fellow talks but trips over his words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stammers or stutters cannot speak smoothly.

clue.text: He makes love sentimentally or rather keeps quiet

indicators.note: the word for 'rather' holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: 'I'd sooner' means I'd rather
P, piano, means quiet in music

explanation.surface: A romantic softie, or perhaps someone who stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner is also the theme name: the Reverend W.A. Spooner, who swapped sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoon is to court or kiss sentimentally, so one who does so is a spooner.

clue.text: 18's breakable statue's big idea

indicators.note: 18 is Spooner, so the opening sounds of the two words change places

parts.note: plaster breaks easily, describing the figure
a statue is a figure of a man

explanation.surface: A fragile sculpture embodies a grand concept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plaster man' (a breakable statue) with the starts swapped gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A master plan is a grand overall scheme, a big idea.

clue.text: Source of jelly produces 18's carrier's complaint

indicators.note: 18 is Spooner, so the first sounds are swapped between the two words

parts.note: a barrow carries loads
a moan is a complaint

explanation.surface: A gripe about wheelbarrows yields something for jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrowbones are boiled to make stock that sets to a jelly.

clue.text: Victim of sex trafficker causing 18 just a ripple?

indicators.note: 18 is Spooner, so his lips swap the opening sounds

parts.note: slight, as in just a small one
a ripple is a small wave

explanation.surface: A trafficked victim whose plight causes barely a ripple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slight wave' (just a ripple) with its first sounds swapped gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: White slavery was the old term for forced prostitution, and a white slave its victim.

clue.text: See 19
Spode set placed just so

indicators.note: the letters of the china name are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A Spode china set arranged precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: Spode is a brand of English porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Posed means arranged or positioned deliberately, placed just so.

clue.text: A complaint I have with a rodent

parts.note: gout is a painful ailment

explanation.surface: Someone moans of an ailment and a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a burrowing rodent of Central and South America.

clue.text: Makes an unconventional drug for such as 2 will be actually

indicators.note: unconventional means out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Producing an odd drug for the baby on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: A baby is often named after a relative, so it will in truth be someone's namesake.
explanation.definitionFit: A child named after someone shares that person's name and so is their namesake.

clue.text: The majesty of King George with half a continent

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex
and means with

indicators.note: only the first half of the continent's name is taken

explanation.surface: A regal splendour belonging to a king and a continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is imposing magnificence, the quality of majesty.

clue.text: Original song sung by naturists?

parts.note: a new ditty, said aloud, names the unclothed state naturists enjoy

explanation.surface: Nudists perform a freshly composed tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists go unclothed, a state of nakedness, punningly a fresh little song.
